cover.headline: India's TAN leader is about to get much bigger, but a war-time windfall is being priced as if it will last
cover.lead: Deepak Fertilisers makes ~40% of India's technical ammonium nitrate (TAN, the base of mining explosives), most of its concentrated nitric acid, its own ammonia (500 ktpa at Taloja) and Mahadhan fertilisers. Two projects worth ~₹4,650 cr (Gopalpur TAN, Dahej nitric acid) are due to start in Q2FY27 (we assume output from Q3), and a 15-year Equinor gas contract began in May-2026. Q1FY27 was a record (EBITDA ₹845 cr, 26% margin) because the Middle East war pushed ammonia to ~$800/t and TAN to ~₹70/kg. Those prices were already falling by end-September. We forecast EPS of ₹110.0 / 109.7 / 115.4 for FY27-29E: higher volumes roughly offset fading spreads. The street (Emkay) values the stock on a **sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA**; we do the same on Sep-28E: Chemicals at **7x** and Fertilisers at **6x** (from the stock's own forward-multiple history, de-rated with the sector), less corporate costs, the DMSL convertible holders' claim and net debt. That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** P/E (₹957 at 8.5x) and DCF (₹1,436) bracket it. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A real TAN franchise that grows 64% in capacity
arguments.p: TAN volumes rose from 519 kt (FY25) to 577 kt (FY26) at ~98% utilisation; Gopalpur adds 376 ktpa on the east coast, next to the coal belt, taking capacity to ~963 ktpa. Deepak is the only Indian maker of low- and high-density AN, sells 17% of TAN revenue through mine-site services (B2C) and has bought an explosives unit (Chardham, ₹121 cr). Dahej adds 450 ktpa of nitric acid, 65% of the concentrated grade pre-sold for 20 years.

arguments.h: Q1FY27 was a windfall, not a run-rate
arguments.p: Chemicals EBIT was ₹805 cr in Q1FY27, 70% of the segment's full-year FY26 EBIT (₹1,147 cr). Ammonia (bulk FOB Middle East) went from ~$300/t in mid-2025 to $801/t in May-2026; it was ~$600 by end-July and Tampa ammonia fell for a fourth month in September. We put Chemicals EBITDA margins at 37.5% in FY27E and 32% in FY28E (47% in Q1), still above FY25's 33% thanks to cheaper Equinor gas.

arguments.h: Debt falls from FY28, with strings attached
arguments.p: Net debt was ₹4,719 cr at Jun-26 (company measure). Capex drops from ~₹950 cr (FY27E) to ~₹500-600 cr and we see net debt at ~₹2,590 cr by Mar-29E (Screener basis). But the ₹800 cr of DMSL convertibles carry a 12.5% yield and will take ~6-7% of the mining subsidiary; a promoter LLP bought ₹300 cr of them partly with money borrowed against pledged DFPCL shares; and the ammonia subsidiary lost ₹257 cr in FY26.

arguments.h: The price already pays for the good news
arguments.p: At ₹1,351 the stock trades at 12.3x our FY28E EPS and 7.2x FY28E EV/EBITDA. Its own one-year-forward medians since Apr-2021 are 9.7x P/E (ex-FY24 trough) and 6.8x EV/EBITDA, and fertiliser and chemical peers sit below their five-year medians. Our sum of the parts implies 6.8x Sep-28E EBITDA. Upside needs the war-time spreads to last.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): commissioning of Gopalpur and Dahej (guided for Q2FY27, after three slips) and how far spreads fell from Q1.
Rabi 2026-27 nutrient-based subsidy rates (not announced by 30-Sep-2026): whether they cover phosphoric acid at ~$1,360/t and sulphur.
Ammonia and TAN prices: Russian supply (export ban lifted in May-2026; analysts flagged a possible ammonia export ban from October-2026) and Middle East shipping.
Gopalpur ramp-up: management targets ~80% utilisation by Q4FY27; ammonia for Gopalpur is bought, not made.
DMSL listing (IPO or demerger, no decision yet) and the CCD conversion (by mutual agreement after ~30 months, i.e. from late 2027; mandatory at 48 months).

sections.title: What Deepak does: turns gas into ammonia, ammonia into explosives-grade nitrate, acids and fertilisers

blocks.p: Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals (DFPCL) started in 1979 as an ammonia-based chemicals and fertiliser maker at Taloja, near Mumbai. Today it runs one value chain: natural gas (a domestic take-or-pay contract and, since May-2026, a 15-year LNG contract with Equinor of Norway) → ammonia (a 500 ktpa plant at Taloja, plus bought and traded ammonia) → nitric acid (885 ktpa weak, 231 ktpa concentrated) → technical ammonium nitrate (TAN, 587 ktpa), the oxidiser in mining and quarrying explosives. Alongside sit isopropyl alcohol (IPA, 70 ktpa, made from refinery propylene) for pharma solvents, and Mahadhan crop nutrition: complex fertilisers (NP 24:24:0, NPK), crop-specific Croptek blends, Bensulf and water-soluble fertilisers sold mainly in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. Despite the name, fertilisers are 54% of revenue but only ~27% of segment profit; chemicals are the profit engine.

blocks.callout: **Pattern to remember:** Deepak builds big integrated assets and then lives through the commodity cycle on them. The ammonia plant arrived as ammonia prices fell (FY24) and lost money in its own books in FY26; it is earning well only now, in a war. Gopalpur arrives as TAN prices are at a peak. The assets are real, but timing has rarely been kind, and both projects ran late and over their first budgets.

sections.title: Industry: TAN is short in India, ammonia is volatile, fertilisers are run by policy

blocks.p: **TAN.** India used ~1,319 kt of TAN in FY25 but made only ~916 kt and imported ~422 kt, mostly from Russia (Emkay, citing industry data). Demand follows coal and mineral output and infrastructure blasting; Q2 (monsoon) is the weak quarter and Q4 the strongest. In early 2026 Russian exports were disrupted (an export ban, lifted in May-2026, and plant incidents), which is why domestic prices jumped. New supply is coming: Deepak's own Gopalpur (376 ktpa) and, further out, Coal India's coal-gasification-based ammonium nitrate, whose technology is still unproven. **Ammonia.** Global ammonia rose from ~$300/t (mid-2025) to $801/t (May-2026) on Middle East supply losses and was falling again by September. **Fertilisers.** Phosphatic and potassic fertilisers are paid a per-kg Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) fixed each season, and the government keeps farm-gate prices in check: if phosphoric acid and sulphur rise faster than the subsidy, NPK makers' margins shrink, as in FY24 and H2FY26.

sections.title: Chemicals: a strong TAN and nitric acid franchise, with Q1FY27 profits that will not last

blocks.p: The Chemicals segment (TAN, nitric acid, IPA, ammonia and Australian blasting services) earned EBIT of ₹1,412 cr in FY25 and ₹1,147 cr in FY26 on revenue of ~₹5,100-5,300 cr, i.e. EBITDA margins of 33% and 27% once segment depreciation is added back. **TAN** is the core: 577 kt sold in FY26 (+11%) at ~98% utilisation, ₹2,604 cr of revenue, 16-17% of it from mine-site services and bulk-explosive supply (B2C), which earn more than selling bags of nitrate. **Industrial chemicals** (₹1,842 cr): 302 kt of merchant nitric acid (~45% of India's merchant market per the annual report) and 63 kt of IPA; IPA depends on refinery propylene, which the government diverted to LPG during the 2026 gas crisis, so Q1FY27 IPA volumes fell 76%. **Ammonia**: the Taloja plant made 452 kt in FY26 (~93% of group needs) and was debottlenecked ~10% in the Q4FY26 shutdown; in its own books (PCL) it lost ₹257 cr after interest and depreciation, because it sells to group plants at internal prices. In Q1FY27 everything turned: segment EBIT ₹805 cr on ₹1,882 cr (42.8%).

blocks.callout: **What we assume and why.** FY27E: Q1 as reported, then ~34% margins for Q2-Q4 (ammonia already ~$600/t by end-July vs ~$800 in May-June; a full quarter of Equinor gas from Q2; Gopalpur and Dahej from H2). FY28E: TAN at ~₹50/kg and ~₹16,000/t of EBITDA on 880 kt (Emkay assumed ~₹14,500/t before the war), ammonia ~₹550 cr, blasting ~₹120 cr, industrial chemicals ~₹600 cr = ~32%. **Sensitivity:** every ₹1/kg of TAN margin on 880 kt moves FY28E EPS by ~₹5.2; holding Q1FY27's ~47% Chemicals margin through FY28E would add roughly ₹1,200 cr of EBITDA. Our bull case assumes only part of that (+4 points of margin).

sections.title: Fertilisers: half the revenue, a fifth of the profit, and the subsidy calendar decides the margin

blocks.p: Mahadhan AgriTech sells ~₹6,200 cr a year of fertilisers: manufactured NP and NPK grades (NPK 494 kt and nitrophosphate 241 kt in FY26, both lower than FY25 as plants ran at ~54-75%), Croptek crop-specific blends (248 kt), Bensulf and water-soluble products, and ~₹1,760 cr of traded DAP/MOP. Specialty products and Croptek were 33% of segment revenue in FY26 and 43% in Q1FY27. Segment EBIT was ₹425 cr in FY25 and ₹420 cr in FY26 (6.8%), but only ₹44 cr in Q1FY27 (3.2%): phosphoric acid was $1,360/t (+18% YoY), sulphur costs cut Bensulf volumes 44%, rains were late, and the Kharif subsidy (+12% in outlay) did not cover the cost increase. The government held DAP and urea prices before state elections, which capped the premium Deepak could charge on NPKs (CMD, May-2026).

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a decent regional brand in a policy-set market. When subsidies track costs (FY21-23, FY25) it earns 7-10% EBITDA margins; when they lag (FY24, Q1FY27) it earns close to nothing. We assume 5.5% for FY27E and a return to 7.5-8% in FY28-29E, below FY25. The fertiliser business also ties up working capital: ₹751 cr of subsidy was owed by the government at Mar-26 (₹619 cr a year earlier), which is one reason FY26 operating cash flow was so weak.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** the projects are real and nearly finished; the risk now is the ramp-up and the margin, not the construction. Gopalpur arrives into a TAN market that was short in 2026 but will loosen as Russian supply returns and new Indian capacity comes, and it buys ammonia at market prices. We therefore model a gradual fill (~80% by FY28E) and a lower margin than Taloja's.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: a real TAN position, no pricing power

verdicts: ~40% of India's TAN; the only Indian maker of low-density, high-density and medical-grade AN; west and (from FY27) east coast plants; long ties with Coal India, explosives makers and contractors; B2C/mine-site services 17% of TAN revenue.
Own 500 ktpa ammonia and a 15-year Henry Hub-linked LNG contract cut costs vs buying spot; but the ammonia subsidiary lost Rs257 cr in FY26 and Gopalpur will run on bought ammonia.
TAN, nitric acid, IPA and ammonia follow global prices and imports (Rs45/kg TAN in FY26, Rs70/kg in Q1FY27); fertiliser prices are effectively set by subsidy policy.
Mahadhan is strong in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat; specialty + Croptek ~40% of segment revenue; but segment EBITDA margins of 0-10% show a subsidy-dependent NPK business.
Largest nitric acid maker in South/South-East Asia (62% of India's CNA); 65% of the new Dahej CNA tied up for 20 years.
Ammonia plant cost ~50% over first estimates (Emkay); Gopalpur slipped three times; promoter-linked financing (CCDs, OCDs).

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Deepak has a **position**, not a moat. In TAN it is the largest Indian producer with the widest product range, plants on both coasts from FY27 and growing mine-site services; in concentrated nitric acid it has most of the market and long contracts. That wins volume and customers. It does not set prices: TAN, nitric acid, IPA and ammonia follow global prices and imports, and fertiliser economics are set by the subsidy. Returns show it: ROCE ran 11-25% over FY22-26 and Chemicals segment pre-tax ROCE fell from 72% (FY23) to 26.3% (FY26) as capital went into projects. We give no moat premium in the multiple.

sections.title: Quarters: three weak ones, then a ₹845 cr record in Q1FY27 on war-time prices

blocks.p: Quarterly EBITDA ran at ₹460-515 cr through FY25 and Q1FY26, slid to ₹353-354 cr in Q3-Q4FY26 (fertiliser costs ahead of subsidies, weak IPA, the ammonia turnaround), and then jumped to ₹845 cr in Q1FY27. The jump came from the Chemicals segment (EBIT ₹805 cr, 43% of its revenue): ammonia traded at ~$780-800/t FOB Middle East in May-June 2026, TAN realisations rose to ~₹70/kg (₹45/kg in FY26) as imports dried up, and the first Equinor LNG cargo (May-2026) lowered gas cost. Fertilisers earned only ₹44 cr. TAN volumes actually fell 12% (a PESO licensing-portal change) and IPA volumes 76% (propylene curtailed by the government).

blocks.callout: **So what:** do not annualise Q1FY27. Management itself called Q2 seasonally soft (monsoon cuts blasting), ammonia was already back near $600/t by the end of July and Tampa ammonia fell for a fourth month in September. We assume ~₹670 cr of EBITDA a quarter for Q2-Q4FY27: lower spreads, offset by a full quarter of Equinor gas and the first output from Gopalpur and Dahej. Q2FY27 results are due by mid-November 2026.

sections.title: Revenue tripled in a decade; profit has followed global ammonia, not a rising line

blocks.p: Revenue rose from ₹3,808 cr in FY15 to ₹11,506 cr in FY26, but in jumps and falls: +47% in FY23 when the Russia-Ukraine war lifted ammonia, nitric acid and fertiliser prices, −23% in FY24 when they fell back, +18% and +12% in FY25-26. EBITDA tells the same story: ₹961 cr (FY21), ₹2,165 cr at the FY23 peak, ₹1,287 cr in FY24, ₹1,925 cr in FY25 and ₹1,684 cr in FY26, when phosphoric acid, sulphur and a planned ammonia shutdown (~₹75 cr) hurt. Below EBITDA the 500 ktpa ammonia plant changed the cost base: depreciation went from ₹233 cr (FY22) to ₹424 cr and interest from ₹155 cr to ₹404 cr (FY24), ₹353 cr in FY26 only because ₹116 cr was capitalised into the new projects. Then Q1FY27 broke every record: EBITDA ₹845 cr (26% margin) and profit ₹490 cr, two-thirds of FY26's full-year profit in one quarter.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a spread business. Deepak buys gas, ammonia, phosphoric acid, sulphur and propylene and sells products whose prices follow global benchmarks (TAN, nitric acid, IPA, ammonia) or government subsidy rates (fertilisers). Profit therefore moves with global spreads, as FY23-FY24 and now Q1FY27 show. What management controls is volume (Gopalpur and Dahej add ~64% to TAN and ~40% to nitric acid capacity), cost (own ammonia, the Equinor gas contract) and mix (B2C mining services, specialty fertilisers). Our forecasts lean on those, not on the war-time spreads lasting.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but capitalised interest, state incentives and a convertible shown as equity flatter the picture

bullets: **Capitalised interest.** ₹116 cr of FY26 interest (₹41 cr in FY25) was added to the cost of Gopalpur and Dahej instead of the P&L (gross interest ₹425 cr vs ₹353 cr reported). It stops at start-up, so FY27-28 interest rises even if debt falls; we model ₹430 cr for FY27E.

**State incentives inside revenue.** Gujarat and Maharashtra investment incentives of ₹109 cr (FY26) and ₹204 cr (FY25) are booked as revenue, i.e. inside EBITDA; ₹403 cr was still receivable from the states at Mar-26. Emkay estimated the GST cut (18% → 5%) lowers the Maharashtra incentive by ₹120-140 cr a year.
**Other income is not all recurring.** FY26 other income of ₹103 cr included ₹17 cr of interest on a tax refund, ₹20 cr of mutual-fund gains and ₹28 cr of hedging gains; we forecast only ₹30-40 cr.

**A convertible shown as equity.** DMSL's ₹800 cr CCDs pay 8% in cash, target a 12.5% annual return and carry an investor put on specified events, yet ₹619 cr of them sits in equity (as minority interest) and only ₹181 cr in debt. Economically, net debt is understated by up to ~₹619 cr; we deduct that amount in our valuation.

**Transfer prices hide where the profit is.** The ammonia subsidiary sells to group plants at internal prices and lost ₹257 cr in FY26; TAN and nitric acid show the benefit. The company does not report ammonia, TAN and industrial-chemical profit separately.

**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was ₹206 cr in FY26 on EBITDA of ₹1,684 cr (₹1,880 cr in FY25), as receivables rose ₹728 cr (incl. subsidy ₹751 cr owed by the government) and inventory ₹669 cr. Management called it a temporary Kharif build-up.
**One-offs.** Q4FY26: ~₹70-75 cr ammonia turnaround and ₹20 cr labour-code charge. FY25: a one-time tax credit of ₹40 cr.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** P G Bhagwat LLP gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter; key audit matters were the CCD accounting and contingent liabilities. Seven subsidiaries holding ₹10,613 cr of assets were audited by other firms, database-level audit trails ran only from Oct-2025, and CARO remarks cover cash losses at PCL. We see no sign of manipulation, but reported EBITDA includes state incentives, interest was capitalised during construction, and the CCD treatment makes leverage look lower than it is.

sections.title: Net debt peaked near ₹4,800 cr; the projects are paid for, the cash has to follow

blocks.p: Two building cycles explain the debt. The ammonia plant took net debt from ~₹1,500 cr (FY22) to ~₹3,500 cr (FY24); Gopalpur and Dahej (FY25-27) took it to ₹4,824 cr at Mar-26 on the company's measure (₹5,001 cr on Screener's, which also counts ₹184 cr of leases and the ₹181 cr debt part of DMSL's CCDs). FY26 was a poor cash year: operating cash flow was only ₹206 cr on ₹1,684 cr of EBITDA because receivables rose by ₹728 cr (subsidy due from the government ₹751 cr, up from ₹619 cr) and inventory by ₹669 cr. Q1FY27's profits brought net debt down to ₹4,719 cr (1.4x annualised EBITDA) even after ₹515 cr of capex. Over FY19-26 Deepak generated ₹7,658 cr of operating cash and spent ₹7,199 cr on plants.

sections.title: Our forecasts: EBITDA up 70% by FY28E, but EPS flat at ~₹110-115 after the Q1 windfall

blocks.p: We model the two reported segments. **Chemicals** revenue is built from TAN volume × realisation (650 / 880 / 930 kt at ₹58 / 50 / 48 per kg), industrial chemicals (₹2,130 / 2,550 / 2,700 cr with Dahej) and ammonia/blasting/other sales (₹1,500 / 1,300 / 1,300 cr), with EBITDA margins of 37.5% / 32% / 31%. **Fertilisers** grow 2% / 6% / 6% at 5.5% / 7.5% / 8% margins. Corporate costs (net of the other income booked in segment results) are ₹260-280 cr. Below EBITDA: depreciation steps up as the ~₹4,650 cr of new plant starts (₹600-680 cr), interest rises to ₹430 cr in FY27E once capitalisation stops and then falls with debt (₹400 / 310 cr), tax 25.5%, payout 17-20%. Capex ₹950 / 500 / 600 cr. Every input is on the Excel model's Assumptions sheet, which recalculates this report's target.

sections.title: The street: thin coverage, one Neutral and one stale Buy

blocks.p: Only two brokers had published calls we could find standing on 30-Sep-2026: **Keynote Capitals Neutral ₹1,534** (3-Jun-2026, after Q4FY26; it had a Buy at ₹1,317 in Feb-2026, which the stock passed) and **Emkay Global BUY ₹2,000** (initiation, 18-Nov-2025; no later Emkay note was found). Trendlyne's consensus on 5-May-2026 showed a ₹1,815 target from two calls. The bulls (Emkay) argue that Gopalpur, Dahej and the Equinor contract lift EBITDA by more than 50% over FY26-28E and that listing DMSL would reveal its value (Emkay put DMSL alone at more than the whole company's market value). The caution (Keynote's downgrade; our view) is about price: the stock had already rallied from ~₹1,044 (Feb-2026) to ~₹1,400-1,650 by mid-2026 on war-time spreads.

Promoter-linked financing: a promoter LLP bought Rs300 cr of DMSL CCDs (8% coupon, 12.5% XIRR, put option) partly with money borrowed against pledged DFPCL shares; a promoter company holds Rs151 cr of DFPCL OCDs; MAL committed Rs75 cr to an AIF run by a promoter company.
Fertiliser margins depend on NBS rates keeping up with phosphoric acid and sulphur; Rabi 2026-27 rates were still pending on 30-Sep-2026 and the monsoon was deficient.
Gopalpur is not backward integrated, so it is exposed to imported ammonia prices and logistics; new domestic TAN capacity could pressure prices.
Cash conversion was poor in FY26: operating cash Rs206 cr on EBITDA Rs1,684 cr, as receivables (incl. Rs751 cr of subsidy) and inventory rose.
Pay is high for the size of the company: the CMD drew Rs31.3 cr from the parent in FY26 (4% of consolidated attributable profit), Rs20 cr of it outside salary and commission.

sections.title: Valuation: a sum of the parts at 6.8x Sep-28E EBITDA gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}

blocks.h: How the street values Deepak Fertilisers

blocks.p: Coverage is thin. The only detailed method we found is Emkay's (initiation, 18-Nov-2025): a **sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA** for Dec-27E, with the mining subsidiary DMSL (TAN, ammonia, Australian blasting) at 12x, industrial chemicals at 10x and crop nutrition at 6x, ~10x overall, for a ₹2,000 target. Emkay set 12x for DMSL below the ~17x at which its ₹800 cr convertibles were priced. Keynote Capitals moved to Neutral with a ₹1,534 target on 3-Jun-2026 (method not visible to us); FundsIndia used 17x FY27E P/E in Aug-2025. A sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA is the right tool here: the businesses differ in quality, debt is material, and management intends to list DMSL and MAL separately. We use the company's reported segments (Chemicals, Fertilisers) because profit by legal entity is not disclosed quarterly.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good franchise at a peak, with a price that assumes the peak lasts

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest maker of technical ammonium nitrate (~40% share, going to ~963 ktpa), its main concentrated nitric acid supplier, a 500 ktpa ammonia plant fed by a 15-year LNG contract, and a regional fertiliser brand (Mahadhan) whose margins depend on subsidy policy. The heavy spending is almost over; from FY28 the company should generate ₹1,200-1,400 cr of free cash a year in our base case.

**What you are paying:** ₹1,351 is 12.3x our FY28E EPS (₹109.7) and 7.2x FY28E EV/EBITDA, against own one-year-forward medians of 9.7x P/E and 6.8x EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021. Our FY28E EBITDA (₹2,870 cr) already includes Gopalpur, Dahej and Equinor and still-elevated spreads; EPS is flat over FY27-29E because Q1FY27's windfall does not repeat. Our sum of the parts (Chemicals 7x, Fertilisers 6x; 6.8x overall) gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}: **SELL**.

blocks.callout: **How we would act.** Our rating follows the house rule (Our ratings follow the upside to our 12−month target: BUY at +15% or more, HOLD between −5% and +15%, SELL below −5%.). At ₹1,351 the target of {{dcf.tp|inr}} implies {{dcf.upside|chg}}: **SELL**. At our target, the rating would move to HOLD if the price fell below ~₹1,240 and to BUY below ~₹1,030; we would raise the target if Q2-Q3FY27 show spreads holding while Gopalpur fills. The bull case ({{scen.bull.tp|inr}}) is real: it needs war-time spreads to last another year. The bear case ({{scen.bear.tp|inr}}) is FY24 again with more capacity.
